content:
Local weather is one of the most underrated variables in your Apple Home smart home automation setup. Over the past few years, I've used sensors for all sorts of things, from reminding me to let faucets drip during freezing weather, to adjusting sprinkler schedules with Eve Aqua during hot days. Eve Weather has been part of my setup for a while, and after being upgraded to support Matter a few years ago, it has really worked brilliantly at my home.

HomeKit Weekly is a series focused on smart home accessories, automation tips, and everything related to the Apple smart home framework.

If you've been following HomeKit Weekly, you'll know I'm a big fan of fully hands-off automations. The value of smart home accessories lies in their ability to run automatically, which is exactly why I've always recommended building your smart home around a single ecosystem rather than mixing and matching different brands all over the place. Even in the age of Matter, I don't want to deal with a ton of different platforms. For me, the answer is Apple Home. I love using Eve's devices because they've always prioritised privacy — if you stick to local control with Matter, you don't need to register for a cloud account. Eve has also been very proactive in supporting Matter and Thread over the past few years, which is exactly what we all want to see.

Eve Weather packs three data points into one compact device: temperature, humidity, and barometric pressure. It carries an IPX4 water resistance rating, and the aluminium housing looks like it was made to live outdoors. Mine is mounted outside, and it provides readings that are very close to local conditions, typically a few degrees off from what the Apple Weather app reports. Honestly, this difference matters a lot, especially when the weather is extremely hot or extremely cold. When your pipes are freezing at 31°F (-0.6°C) but the app tells you it's 34°F (1.1°C), you'll be very glad you installed this local sensor.

One of the underrated features of Eve Weather is the built-in 12-hour weather trend display. It uses barometric pressure changes to forecast weather trends, showing you a visual icon indicating whether it's likely to be clear, cloudy, rainy, or stormy. This small detail is incredibly useful — you can take it in at a glance without even opening your phone app.

Here are a few automation examples you can set up with Eve Weather:

  • When the temperature drops below freezing, turn on a coloured light to remind everyone at home to let the faucets drip.
  • When outdoor humidity is particularly high, automatically switch on the dehumidifier.
  • If it has already rained and more rain is forecast, delay the sprinkler system from running.
  • Without leaving the house, just ask Siri what the temperature is in the garden outside.

Matter and Thread Support in 2026

A few years ago, Eve rolled out a free firmware update that brought Matter support to Eve Weather. If you already have an Eve Weather, you can update it through the Eve app. The Matter version supports Apple Home as well as Amazon Alexa, Google Home, and SmartThings. The sensor itself is identical — it just becomes cross-platform, so if you ever want to switch to a different smart home ecosystem in the future, there's no issue at all.

Eve Weather is what's known as a Minimal Thread Device, meaning it can communicate using Thread but won't relay data for other devices. That job is left to Full Thread Devices that are mains-powered, such as the Eve Energy or Eve Water Guard. The more Full Thread Devices you have, the stronger and more stable your Thread network becomes, and battery-powered devices like Eve Weather can directly benefit from that stability.

You still don't need to register for an Eve account at all — everything is handled locally, unless you choose otherwise. The Eve iPhone app is a really handy tool for visualising and tracking historical trends in temperature, barometric pressure, and humidity. It's a fascinating way to spot patterns, helping you make smarter decisions about when to water the lawn or manage energy use.

I've placed a few HomePod minis around the house, backed by an Eero 6E network to support Thread. The Eero software has Thread support built in, so it provides a solid foundation for accessories like Eve Weather, ensuring a stable connection with quick response times.

Eve Weather Final Verdict

The only improvement I'd still like to see is a rechargeable battery. The battery lasts roughly several months, but I'd much prefer a USB-C port like the Eve Room has. Setting that aside, Eve Weather is one of my favourite Apple Home accessories. It's simple, looks great, and thanks to Matter, works brilliantly across all the major platforms. If you're looking to bring local weather data into your smart home and use it to trigger useful automations, Eve Weather is an easy recommendation for me.

You can pick one up from Amazon or directly from the Eve Store.
